Bethesda says their newest game is complete and are spending a few months testing for bugs, is this normal or above average?
How long is the average length of the testing for bugs phase during development?

Thats normal. I have worked on bug testing before and it can stretch to months because the cycle isn't just find find find. Its find, verify, change ingame, retest both that original issue and if it causes additional ones. And move on.
Varies depending on the complexity of the software.

That should be determined by how small a chunk of 'development' you would be testing, what the testing success criteria are (that also equal what the devs should have developed) combined with what tooling you use and how long a full regression is - if its needed. Testing should continue for the life of the development. Not chunking it up into smaller pieces so dev and test are very VERY close together raises arbitrary barriers to delivery speed and combined dev/test value.

When you are writing software, you often spend a decent amount of time working on bugs throughout the development process in one way or another. However, yes. Once software is feature-complete, a responsible developer will likely test it to figure out where it breaks. Not all games do this very well or at all, but I'd say most do it to a greater or lesser extent.
